evidence.note: Explicitly chose a monolithic approach: 'I'll write the entire decoder in one go based on knowledge of zstd, then iterate on bugs.' No plan to land verifiable subsystems incrementally.

Code written as sequential append chunks (bit readers → FSE → Huffman → literals → sequences → block/frame → dictionary). The construction order loosely respects dependencies, but each chunk is just 'write more code' with no done-condition; none is compiled or tested in isolation.
First build/test happens only AFTER the entire ~1000-line decoder is written — confirming nothing was verifiable until everything was done, the exact failure mode the dimension warns about.
The only 'done-signal' is the aggregate test.sh (6 inputs) at the very end; no per-subsystem or smallest-possible test inputs, no walking-skeleton (raw blocks/raw literals) checkpoint was staged.

reasoning: The agent read the RFC subsystem-by-subsystem and its code chunks loosely follow the true dependency order (FSE before Huffman before sequences before dictionaries), showing more than zero awareness. But it explicitly committed to writing the whole decoder in one monolithic pass and only compiled/tested after everything was written, so no component was independently checkable and milestones amounted to 'write the next chunk.' There is no walking-skeleton path, no per-subsystem test input, and no explicit per-milestone done-condition — matching anchor 3 (vague ordering in the head, entangled components) rather than the landed-and-checkpointed behavior of anchor 5.
